title: What Is a Computer?

scenes.say: Quick question. How many computers do you think you own?
There's the laptop, sure. But also your phone. Your TV. Your car. Your microwave, probably. Maybe even your thermostat.
Today on Tech from Scratch: what is a computer, really?
Here's the simple version. A computer is a machine that takes in information, works on it, remembers it, and gives you a result. That's it. Four jobs.
The easiest way to picture it is a kitchen.
First, ingredients come in. For a computer, that's input: what you type, tap, click, or say. Your keyboard, your touchscreen, your microphone.

card.title: INPUT: what you type, tap, click or say

scenes.say: Next, someone has to cook. That's the processor, sometimes called the CPU. It follows instructions, step by step, incredibly fast. Billions of tiny steps every second.

card.sub: Billions of tiny steps every second

scenes.say: While the cook works, they need counter space. That's memory, or RAM. It holds whatever you're working on right now. More counter space means you can juggle more at once.

card.sub: It holds what you're working on right now

scenes.say: But here's the catch. When you turn the computer off, the counter gets wiped clean.
That's why there's a pantry. That's storage: your hard drive or SSD. It keeps your photos, files, and apps safe, even when the power's off.

card.title: STORAGE: kept even when the power's off

scenes.say: Finally, the meal is served. That's output: what you see on the screen, hear from the speakers, or get from the printer.

card.title: OUTPUT: what you see, hear, or print

scenes.say: So when you send a text: your thumbs are the input, the processor does the work, memory holds the message while you type, storage saves the conversation, and the screen shows it sent. Every computer, from a phone to a supercomputer, does those same four jobs.
Ingredients in. Cook works. Counter holds. Pantry keeps. Meal comes out. That's a computer.
Next time, we'll open one up and look at the parts that make all this happen. Subscribe so you don't miss it, and we'll see you then.

shorts.hook: You own more computers than you think

description: What actually counts as a computer? Kip and Bub explain the four jobs every computer does, using a kitchen: ingredients in, a cook, counter space, a pantry, and a meal served.
